_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for PEP retrospectives (retro/build_pep.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2008 were accepted during the session on their release days, and from 2009 most came before the open (each print's release_time says which). The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the latest guide for the current fiscal year (display only, except a fiscal-year net revenue guide in constant currency in numbers, 'rev_guide': every PepsiCo EPS guide of 2007-2016 is a one-sided bound, words, or a figure or range on the core basis, which removes the recurring commodity mark-to-market impact), and the latest declared dividend. PepsiCo's fiscal year ends on the last Saturday of December (53 weeks in 2011 and 2016). Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, and a company figure excluding one-offs only replaces GAAP EPS (the history's 'normalization' says which). A print's margins and growth rates are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw'; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago inventories come from the year-ago quarter's own release, an operating profit on a comparable basis that excludes one-offs only replaces GAAP, and lc_pct is the net revenue growth excluding currency that the release states, else the reported growth it states less the currency effect the release or the quarter's 10-Q states (the reported growth where no filing states one); acquisitions, divestitures (the Venezuela deconsolidation among them) and the extra week stay in, as published, and organic growth, which removes them, is not used. A print whose release states no total servings takes them from the first later filing that does ('servings_later'), on that filing's own date. rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'PEP'): the ten annual values FY1997-FY2006 (the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04), each change from the latest 10-K published by then that reports both years (income statements for the margins, the five-year summary for net revenue), the inventory gap within each year's own 10-K; total servings growth from the latest 10-K that states it, first stated for 2000 (FY2001 10-K), so seven values (the AVGO rule: the years the filings report). A company figure excluding one-offs replaces the reported one where the company published it for both years on the same basis: 1997 and 1998 operating margin on ongoing operating profit (FY1998 10-K, excluding unusual items); 2005 and 2006 net revenue excluding the 53rd week of 2005 ($32,144M, Q4 2005 and Q4 2006 releases); 2005 gross margin and 2006 gross and operating margins on the Q4 2006 release's comparable basis. Everything else as reported, seams included (the 1999 bottling deconsolidation, the 2001 Quaker pooling, the EITF 01-9 and 2005 cost reclassifications).
